title: Web UI flow edit: frontend payload to server setattr handler
answers: How does the web UI send response edits to the server?
Why did editing reason phrase not take effect?
body:
Edit path for HTTP flow fields in web UI:
- `web/src/js/components/FlowView/HttpMessages.tsx` (response status line: http_version / status_code / reason editors) → `flowActions.update(flow, { response: {...} })`.
- Server: `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` flow PUT handler loops `for k, v in b.items()` for `request`/`response`, mapping keys to attributes via setattr / explicit branches.
- Keys the server accepts for response: `http_version`, `code` (-> `status_code`), `reason` (formerly buggy `msg`, no longer accepted), `headers`, `trailers`, `content`. Unknown keys raise APIError(400).
- Serialization (flow_to_json in app.py) emits `status_code` and `reason`, but the update payload uses `code`; names differ between read and write.
- Test: `test/mitmproxy/tools/web/test_app.py` update test (PUT /flows/42) sends `reason` and asserts on `f.response.reason`.
invalidReason: Code snippets provided are incomplete — missing the PUT handler in app.py and the update test in test_app.py, which are central to the note's claims about server-side key mapping and test assertions

history.reason: contradicted in session d9ec4539-b1de-4d4c-879c-d0a80836f96a: Before the edit, app.py accepted "msg" not "reason", the test used "msg"/f.response.msg; agent removed msg (now 400), so 'reason (alias msg kept)' and the test claim were wrong pre-change.
